technical_errors: Step 3 (lines 124-139) asks the reader to derive total runs, tier wall-clock as first-submit-to-last-completion, core-hours summed over ALL runs, and 'if the source carries timestamps, peak concurrency' — all whole-file aggregates — from an accounting export the retrieval budget itself describes as running to 'roughly 1500 lines' (line 68), using only the 2 Greps + 3 windowed Reads of ~120 lines the allocation table grants that step (line 81: 'step 3, two Greps and three windows'). Three windows of ~120 lines covers at most ~360 of ~1500 lines (~24%). A true sum or a true wall-clock span requires every row; peak concurrency specifically requires a sweep-line over every job's start/end interval and cannot be recovered from a partial contiguous sample — a sample can only ever yield a lower bound, and nothing in step 3 or the Gotchas says the reported peak might be an undercount. This is load-bearing: step 8 and the Gotchas ('Seats are sized on peak concurrency…') build the entire licence-renewal argument on this number, so a silently-undercounted peak produces exactly the overreaching money claim section 8 warns against.

review.open_twice: "Mostly yes for the domain content — the licence-economics reasoning (seats already paid for, peak vs. average, greedy-incremental vs. per-test-unique ranking, coverage-redundant is not bug-redundant) is sharp, technically correct, and matches the pack's voice closely. But a careful senior reader will stall on two things: the title promises 'cost per verified feature' and the procedure never delivers one, and step 3's 'measured baseline' — the thing the whole trimming proposal rests its numeric credibility on — cannot actually be computed accurately from the budget the skill itself grants it. Those two gaps are exactly the kind a principal-level reviewer would catch and lose confidence over, even though the surrounding writing is strong."

fixed: C005 'rank kind: greedy-incremental' / 'per-test-unique' — step 5 now ends with an explicit assignment paragraph ('Write the answer into the block before using it') that reads the ranking report's own header line and sets the token, and states what each token licenses downstream (greedy-incremental licenses a whole-tail proposal, per-test-unique licenses one removal at a time with a named survivor). Step 7 group 2 now cites `rank kind` as the thing that sets removal granularity, so the value is consumed as well as assigned. The third token, `none`, gets its own branch: header silent and engineer cannot say -> `rank kind: none`, report unusable for removals, all candidates come from step 6 instead.

C005 'trim action: fix-and-keep' — added as a real branch in step 7 group 1, not a mention. Where the step 6 waste is a defect in how the run is set up rather than in the test's existence (hang killed at the limit nightly, waveform dumping on by default, duplicate list entry, image rebuilt per test), the recommendation is `fix-and-keep`: the test still runs and still returns the same verdict, only cheaper, so nothing stops being produced and the coverage owner has nothing to weigh. The step also says to prefer `fix-and-keep` over `drop` even at identical saving, because a reviewer reading `drop` against a test they rely on stops reading.

C005 'trim action: stop-collecting' — added as a real, narrowly-guarded branch in step 7: stop a tier collecting coverage while leaving its stimulus running, proposed only where instrumentation is a measured share of a run's cost (`warrant: instrumentation-share`), only where the tier is re-run to hunt bugs rather than close items, and only with a hard precondition named on that candidate's `covered by` line — an instrumented sample still runs at least once per period. This converts the Gotcha that previously argued AGAINST the value into the branch's precondition rather than leaving the two contradicting each other; the Gotcha was rewritten to match.

must_fix / rule 4 — the killed-or-timeout marker is now a declared slot. Step 6 now Greps both in one pass and counts them on two separate lines, with the reason spelled out (a job killed for running long is trimmable; a job that died for want of a licence or disk belongs on another queue).

must_fix / technical_errors / budget_violations — step 3's baseline is now producible inside its own cap. Introduced an explicit affordable whole-file technique in the budget (item 4): a counting Grep that asks for the NUMBER of matching lines rather than the lines, exact at any file size, and declared as the only counted figure the skill may quote over rows nobody read. Step 3 now spends its two Greps in count mode (total runs exact; tier subset exact) and its three windows on first rows / last rows / one interior sample, and states per figure what the windows can support: tier wall clock is readable from the first and last windows ONLY if the export is in submit order (now a fact the Farm accounting slot records), otherwise not-available plus a handoff for the scheduler's own period report; core-hours are explicitly NOT summable from ~20% of a 1500-row export, so the figure is mean-per-run x exact count, marked derived with its sample size, or handed off to CAD for the accounting system's own period total.

must_fix — peak concurrency no longer overreaches. Step 3 now states that peak cannot be recovered from a sample at all (it needs every job's start/end interval; a contiguous window shows only that the peak was AT LEAST what that window held), that a peak counted here is therefore a lower bound and must be written as one, and that a lower bound supports 'we hold at least this many at once' and 'there is a burst' but can never support 'we can free seats'. A handoff is given for the real number (the licence manager's or scheduler's own peak-checkout figure for the period, plus the time it occurred). The `peak` report field now carries the basis, step 8's seat bullet was rewritten to refuse any seat-reduction claim resting on a lower bound (naming who was asked instead), the Gotcha on peak was rewritten to match, and a Human-verification bullet checks that no seat claim anywhere rests on a lower bound.

must_fix — the namesake metric is no longer orphaned. The intro contract and the frontmatter description now promise the figure the title always promised.

Honesty plumbing added so the numbers stay falsifiable rather than merely defensible: a new `baseline basis` field (counted from a counting Grep / sampled per-run cost times that exact count with the sample size / the scheduler's own period total), a rewritten budget coverage rule that demands the statement per figure rather than once per document, and three new Human-verification bullets (every total says whether it was counted, sampled or asked for; the peak line states its basis; the denominator carries its count, dates and source). The author knew to give the Closure record slot a file-or-tracker handoff and did not do the same here, so the skill's most-emphasised safety check — coverage-redundant is not bug-redundant — is the one an agent cannot execute.
